chunks: My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: We were told by Muhammad ibn Idris, and Muhammad ibn Yahya al-‘Attar, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Mansur, from Ahmad ibn Khalid, from Ahmad ibn al-Mubarak, that he said: A man said to Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him: 'There is a narration that is narrated with regards to that a man said to the Commander of the Believers, peace be upon him: “Indeed, I love you.” To which he said to him: “Prepare for poverty a robe.” So he said: It is not as that. He said: He only said to him: “I have prepared for your destitution a robe,” meaning the Day of Resurrection.'
ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali mean when he told the man who said 'I love you' to prepare a robe for poverty?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this variant in *Ma'ani al-Akhbar* to resolve a textual discrepancy regarding Imam Ali’s response to expressions of love (*mawadda*). The correction shifts the meaning from a warning of material destitution to a spiritual assurance that the Imam has already secured a 'garment' of protection and honor for the believer’s specific poverty on the Day of Resurrection. This highlights the Shia emphasis on the intercessory role of the Ahl al-Bayt in alleviating the spiritual vulnerability of their lovers in the Hereafter.
